title: All products

empty_search_body: Try a product name, a part such as receiver or motor, or a size such as 3 inch. Dutch and French part names work too.
help_whoop: There are no whoop-size parts. The smallest OpenDrone build is 3-inch: [see what a 3-inch build needs](/products#build-3-inch). The OpenRX Lite below is a 10.0 × 11.5 mm ExpressLRS receiver with a CRSF output and a 5 V input.
help_video_radio: We do not sell goggles, radios, cameras or video transmitters. Your goggles pair with the video system on the quad: DJI goggles with a DJI O3 or O4 air unit (which one depends on your goggle model, so check DJI's compatibility list first), analog goggles with an analog camera and transmitter. The OpenFrame takes analog, DJI, Walksnail and HDZero video systems. The OpenRX receivers need a radio with an ExpressLRS transmitter; a DJI remote controller cannot. [Which radio to get, and how binding works](/products#coming-from-dji).
help_size: OpenDrone makes 3-inch and 5-inch parts. There is no 7-inch or long-range frame: the largest build is the [5-inch build](/products#build-5-inch). The 30x30 flight controller and ESC mount on 30.5 × 30.5 mm holes, the usual stack pattern on 7-inch frames, and take up to 8S: see the [30x30 flight controller](/products/openfc-lite?Model=30%C3%9730) for its full spec table. For a longer radio link, the OpenRX Mono and Gemini add a sub-GHz band.
help_gps: OpenDrone does not sell a GPS module. See [what a build needs](/products#new-to-fpv).
help_spare: Every part is sold on its own, so a crashed quad needs only the broken part: each flight controller and ESC size, each frame and single motors. Spare arms and plates: [OpenFrame spare parts](/products/openframe-spares), sold out for now. The warranty covers defects, not crash damage: see [Warranty](/warranty).
